note: 喧嘩 is a standard Japanese word for a physical fight as well as a quarrel; the stated physical sense is a normal use.
化学物質 means a chemical substance generally and does not retain the stated artificial-compound restriction; I found no verified JMdict equivalent covering that full definition.
滑る is the ordinary Japanese verb for slipping on a slippery surface; intentional sliding is another use, but the stated loss-of-balance sense is covered.
通夜 is the standard Japanese cultural equivalent for a wake or vigil over the deceased; its local funeral custom is more specific, but it matches the core stated sense.
株式会社 is specifically a stock company. Replace with 法人, whose JMdict entry ent_seq 1517310 sense 0 glosses corporation, corporate body, company, and legal entity.
研究員 suggests an affiliated research staff member. 研究者 is the general researcher term; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1258590 sense 0. Vietnamese nhà nghiên cứu is suitable.
しみ is chiefly a stain or skin blemish. 斑点 better covers a colored or textured spot on an object's surface; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1481340 sense 0.
電子メール and thư điện tử are standard full terms for email as a messaging system.
精神的 is the standard Japanese adjective for mental or relating to the mind; it fits the stated mind-and-mental-activity sense.
演奏 is limited to musical performance. 公演 covers a live public performance more generally; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1273280 sense 0.
近所 usually means the immediate vicinity. 地区 covers a district or area as a division of a municipality or region; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1421020 sense 0.
ストレッチ is the standard Japanese noun for a stretching act or exercise and fits the ordinary physical sense of the definition.
オーバー is an ambiguous shortening. オーバーコート is the full, precise Japanese term; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1032880 sense 0.
消防 naturally names the fire service or department, but the supplied English definition also includes an individual firefighter. No single verified term covers both the organization and person senses.
増進 is mostly an increase in an abstract quality or condition. 増加 is the general noun for increase; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1403160 sense 0.
もっともらしい is directly glossed as plausible and believable and is a standard equivalent for this adjective sense.
輝く is a standard verb for shining or sparkling and its JMdict glosses include glitter.
手本 usually means a model or good example to imitate. 例 covers either a good or bad example; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1585230 sense 0.
何と is the natural Japanese exclamatory equivalent for this use of what, even though the Japanese construction is adverbial.
秘密 has a dictionary sense of secrecy or confidentiality and is a natural noun for the stated hidden condition.
For the stated signature sense used for approval, サイン is the ordinary Japanese word; the autograph label is less usual than this definition.
喧嘩 includes disorderly fighting and brawling in Japanese. It is broader in other contexts, but it covers the core fight sense here.
希望 is a general hope or wish. 志 expresses an aim, ambition, or earnest intention; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1309050 sense 0.
宿泊 describes lodging as an act or stay, while the English and Vietnamese refer to a place. 宿 (やど) has JMdict ent_seq 1337190 senses 0 and 1 for lodging/inn and house/home/dwelling.
論文 is a natural Japanese term for a systematic formal paper or treatise; its JMdict glosses directly include treatise.
叫ぶ and kêu lên both naturally express crying or calling out suddenly, including from strong emotion.
用心 directly covers caution, care, and precaution, matching the definition's prior caution or care to prevent misfortune.
尻 is a natural Japanese term for the rump or hindquarters of an animal as well as a person's behind; the stated animal sense is covered.
輝く is a standard verb for sparkling or reflecting light, and its JMdict glosses include glisten.
不幸 has a Japanese dictionary sense of unhappiness or sorrow, matching the stated emotional condition; the context distinguishes it from a misfortune.
遅刻 is the ordinary Japanese noun for lateness or tardiness and fits the stated state of being late.
はさみ is a standard Japanese term that covers scissors and shears; it fits the described two-bladed cutting tool.
菓子 is the ordinary collective term for confectionery and sweets in Japanese; it is suitable for the stated sweet-food group.
常識 often emphasizes shared knowledge or social norms, while this sense and lẽ thường emphasize sensible judgment. 良識 means good sense; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1554570 sense 0.
示す is show or indicate and is too general for verbally identifying something. 指摘 is a suru-verb meaning pointing out or identifying; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1309940 sense 0.

テレビゲーム is narrower to home-console games and game is broader in Vietnamese. ビデオゲーム is verified in JMdict ent_seq 1105420 sense 0; trò chơi điện tử is a natural full Vietnamese term, though absent from the local frequency list.
構想 is a natural Japanese noun for a plan or conception of something to be done, matching the stated plan-and-intention sense.
責任 covers liability and onus and is a suitable Japanese noun for a legal obligation or burden.
代理 is a generic proxy or substitute. スタンドイン is the specific film-production term for this role; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1069940 sense 0.
香り usually means a pleasant aroma, narrower than a distinctive smell. 匂い covers smell or scent more generally; verified in JMdict ent_seq 1599760 sense 0.
